reference: Documented custom fdisk contracts with independent Python struct/UUID/CRC32 encoders and decoders for small private regular-file images. No util-linux CLI parity is claimed for custom verbs. Source regular-file geometry and write paths skip block-device ioctls. Metadata is separate from operation coverage.
coverage: Bash registration and help metadata only.
Independent MBR image verification, disk ID and free-range lookup.
Private-file MBR creation, slot mutation, boot flag, type, geometry, disk ID and deletion with independent byte checks.
Private-file GPT creation, primary/backup CRC and array consistency, label/UUID/attribute changes.
Private-file extended/logical table creation, insertion/reorder/compact deletion and independent EBR traversal.
Dry-run byte invariance, invalid overlapping-spec rejection, missing private input and pipe-driven quit without writing.
exclusions: No raw/block device, kernel partition request, mount, host path or network operation executes. All image paths are fresh relative regular files.
Real-device kernel partition ioctls remain deferred to a disposable VM or syscall mock.
PTY screen interaction, exhaustive geometry/CRC/error permutations and injected read/write failures remain unqualified; independent image parsers check only the specified fields and invariants.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t reports the registered fdisk loadable as a builtin; this checks availability metadata without entering fdisk.
Bash command -v resolves a builtin by its name even with the candidate executable search path pointing at an empty directory.
Bash help -s exposes the synopsis registered for fdisk; the expected line is the independent short_doc string in fdisk_struct.
cases.stdout: fdisk: fdisk DEV (interactive; or -i DEV) | [--no-act] -l DEV ... | --create-mbr DEV SPEC ... | --create-mbr-extended DEV EXT_SPEC LOGICAL_SPEC ... | --create-gpt DEV SPEC ... | --apply DEV {mbr|gpt} SPEC ... | --delete DEV N | --delete-compact DEV N | --insert-logical DEV START,SIZE[,TYPE[,BOOT]] | --reorder DEV | --set-attrs DEV N ATTRS | --activate DEV N {on|off} | --part-type DEV N TYPE | --set-part DEV N START,SIZE[,TYPE[,BOOT|NAME]] | --part-label DEV N NAME | --part-uuid DEV N UUID | --repair DEV | --verify DEV | --list-free DEV | --list-types | --disk-id DEV [STR]

cases.purpose: Full Bash help advertises MBR, GPT, mutation, and the implemented finite-input editor; metadata only. The stale no-interactive-UI disclaimer is not an operation oracle.
cases.script:
doc=$(help fdisk)
[[ $doc == *"fdisk --create-mbr DEV SPEC [SPEC ...]"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"fdisk --create-gpt DEV SPEC [SPEC ...]"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"fdisk --delete-compact DEV N"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"fdisk --part-uuid DEV N UUID"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"Reads single-letter commands from stdin"* ]]
printf 'help documents MBR, GPT, mutation, and interactive scope\n'

cases.purpose: Cover --partx-kernel BLKPG add/delete/update and post-write partition reread behavior.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM with an isolated throwaway block device or a reviewed ioctl mock that records BLKPG and BLKRRPART requests; the current environment must not issue kernel partition-table ioctls.

cases.purpose: Qualify interactive PTY prompts, key handling and screen restoration; pipe-driven quit has separate runnable coverage.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or reviewed bounded PTY driver with fixed dimensions, a scratch regular-file image, and independently specified terminal transcripts and byte snapshots. Captured pipes cannot establish PTY rendering or terminal restoration.

cases.purpose: Read an independently encoded MBR in a private regular file. Validate verification, disk signature, exact free-range arithmetic, and read-only byte invariance.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
import struct
b=bytearray(2*1024*1024)
struct.pack_into('<I',b,440,0x12345678)
struct.pack_into('<B3sB3sII',b,446,128,bytes(3),131,bytes(3),2048,128)
b[510:512]=b'\x55\xaa'
Path('image.img').write_bytes(b)
Path('before.img').write_bytes(b)
PYC
fdisk --verify image.img
fdisk --disk-id image.img
fdisk --list-free image.img
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
assert Path('image.img').read_bytes()==Path('before.img').read_bytes()
PYC
cases.stdout:
image.img: MBR table validates cleanly
0x12345678
Disk image.img: MBR table free ranges
Device       Start        Sectors     
(free)       2176         1920

cases.purpose: Create and mutate only a fresh private regular-file MBR. Independent public-format decoding checks the final slot, signature, deletion, and every payload byte.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
Path('image.img').write_bytes(bytes(2*1024*1024))
PYC
fdisk --create-mbr image.img 2048,128,linux,boot 2304,64,swap
fdisk --activate image.img 2 on
fdisk --part-type image.img 1 ntfs
fdisk --set-part image.img 1 2048,192
fdisk --disk-id image.img 89abcdef
fdisk --delete image.img 2
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
import struct
b=Path('image.img').read_bytes()
assert len(b)==2*1024*1024 and b[510:512]==b'\x55\xaa'
assert struct.unpack_from('<I',b,440)[0]==0x89abcdef
p=struct.unpack_from('<B3sB3sII',b,446)
assert (p[0],p[2],p[4],p[5])==(0,7,2048,192)
assert b[462:510]==bytes(48)
assert b[512:]==bytes(len(b)-512)
print('MBR fields and payload verified')
PYC

cases.purpose: Create GPT on a private regular file. Independent UUID/struct/CRC32 decoding checks both headers, arrays, type, bounds, label and unchanged partition payload.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
Path('image.img').write_bytes(bytes(2*1024*1024))
PYC
fdisk --create-gpt image.img 2048,128,linux,fixture
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
import struct,zlib,uuid
b=Path('image.img').read_bytes(); sectors=len(b)//512
assert b[510:512]==bytes([0x55,0xaa]) and b[450]==0xee
arrays=[]
for lba,other in [(1,sectors-1),(sectors-1,1)]:
 h=b[lba*512:(lba+1)*512]; assert h[:8]==b'EFI PART'
 size,crc=struct.unpack_from('<II',h,12)
 header=bytearray(h[:size]); header[16:20]=bytes(4)
 assert zlib.crc32(header)==crc
 assert struct.unpack_from('<QQ',h,24)==(lba,other)
 array_lba,count,entry_size,array_crc=struct.unpack_from('<QIII',h,72)
 a=b[array_lba*512:array_lba*512+count*entry_size]
 assert zlib.crc32(a)==array_crc
 arrays.append(a)
assert arrays[0]==arrays[1]
a=arrays[0]
assert uuid.UUID(bytes_le=a[:16])==uuid.UUID('0fc63daf-8483-4772-8e79-3d69d8477de4')
assert struct.unpack_from('<QQ',a,32)==(2048,2175)
assert not any(a[128:])
assert b[2048*512:2176*512]==bytes(128*512)
assert a[56:128].decode('utf-16-le').rstrip('\0')=='fixture'
print('GPT CRCs arrays and payload verified')
PYC
cases.stdout: GPT CRCs arrays and payload verified

cases.purpose: Change label, partition UUID and attributes only in a private image; independent decoding verifies fields plus primary/backup checksums after mutation.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
Path('image.img').write_bytes(bytes(2*1024*1024))
PYC
fdisk --create-gpt image.img 2048,128,linux,fixture
fdisk --part-label image.img 1 renamed
fdisk --part-uuid image.img 1 01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
fdisk --set-attrs image.img 1 4
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
import struct,zlib,uuid
b=Path('image.img').read_bytes(); sectors=len(b)//512
assert b[510:512]==bytes([0x55,0xaa]) and b[450]==0xee
arrays=[]
for lba,other in [(1,sectors-1),(sectors-1,1)]:
 h=b[lba*512:(lba+1)*512]; assert h[:8]==b'EFI PART'
 size,crc=struct.unpack_from('<II',h,12)
 header=bytearray(h[:size]); header[16:20]=bytes(4)
 assert zlib.crc32(header)==crc
 assert struct.unpack_from('<QQ',h,24)==(lba,other)
 array_lba,count,entry_size,array_crc=struct.unpack_from('<QIII',h,72)
 a=b[array_lba*512:array_lba*512+count*entry_size]
 assert zlib.crc32(a)==array_crc
 arrays.append(a)
assert arrays[0]==arrays[1]
a=arrays[0]
assert uuid.UUID(bytes_le=a[:16])==uuid.UUID('0fc63daf-8483-4772-8e79-3d69d8477de4')
assert struct.unpack_from('<QQ',a,32)==(2048,2175)
assert not any(a[128:])
assert b[2048*512:2176*512]==bytes(128*512)
assert a[56:128].decode('utf-16-le').rstrip('\0')=='renamed'
assert uuid.UUID(bytes_le=a[16:32])==uuid.UUID('01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef')
assert struct.unpack_from('<Q',a,48)[0]==4
print('GPT mutations independently verified')
PYC

cases.purpose: Create, insert, reorder and compact-delete two remaining logical entries in a regular-file image; independently traverse EBR relative links and verify payload bytes.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
Path('image.img').write_bytes(bytes(2*1024*1024))
PYC
fdisk --create-mbr-extended image.img 2048,2048,05 2112,128,linux 2560,128,swap
fdisk --insert-logical image.img 2816,64,linux
fdisk --reorder image.img
fdisk --delete-compact image.img 6
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
import struct
b=Path('image.img').read_bytes(); base=2048
assert b[450] in (5,15,133)
seen=set(); lba=base; rows=[]
while True:
 assert lba not in seen; seen.add(lba)
 off=lba*512; assert b[off+510:off+512]==b'\x55\xaa'
 p=struct.unpack_from('<B3sB3sII',b,off+446)
 rows.append((lba+p[4],p[5],p[2]))
 link=struct.unpack_from('<B3sB3sII',b,off+462)
 if not link[2]:break
 lba=base+link[4]
assert rows==[(2112,128,131),(2816,64,131)]
for start,size,_ in rows:assert b[start*512:(start+size)*512]==bytes(size*512)
print('EBR links and payload verified')
PYC

cases.purpose: A small overlapping partition specification is a normal validation error; private image bytes remain untouched.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
Path('image.img').write_bytes(bytes(2*1024*1024))
PYC
if fdisk --create-mbr image.img 2048,128 2100,64; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
b=Path('image.img').read_bytes(); assert b==bytes(2*1024*1024)
print('overlap rejected without writes')
PYC

cases.purpose: The documented extended-container default type is 05 when TYPE is omitted. A fresh private regular-file image should accept the two-field EXT_SPEC; independent decoding verifies the default without using candidate output as the oracle.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
Path('image.img').write_bytes(bytes(2*1024*1024))
PYC
fdisk --create-mbr-extended image.img 2048,2048 2112,128,linux
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
from pathlib import Path
b=Path('image.img').read_bytes()
assert b[450]==5 and b[510:512]==bytes([0x55,0xaa])
print('extended default type verified')
PYC
